This Fiat Ducato Camper Van Shows How You Can Maximize Comfort and Style in a Compact Footprint
17 photos
Photo: SüdBadenVan/miniCampers
Much like the Mercedes-Benz Sprinter dominates the campervan landscape in the United States, the Fiat Ducato serves as the primary backbone of the European campervan market. With its robust build, car-like driveability, boxy, conversion-friendly shape, and generous interior headroom, it stands as the most popular choice when it comes to conversion base vehicles.
The light commercial vehicle is highly prominent across SüdBadenVan’s lineup, and the 2027 Schauinsland 540 camper van shows that even the shortest variant of the Fiat Ducato can be turned into a comfortable living space.
Built for travelers who want their camper van to feel more like a small home than a conventional RV, the Schauinsland 540 preserves an open floor plan and combines it with modern amenities and a cozy country-house-inspired aesthetic that creates a warm, inviting atmosphere, setting it apart from standard, sterile conversions.
SüdBadenVan is a boutique German campervan manufacturer based in Umkirch, near Freiburg. It was founded in 2021 and specializes in transforming standard panel vans into functional, premium mobile homes, with an emphasis on sustainability, minimalism, and practical design. The company’s Schauinsland lineup shows how these principles translate into practice, offering a practical mobile habitat for two people.
Photo: SüdBadenVan/miniCampers The Schauinsland 540 is one of the first floorplans introduced by the German company and is built on the shortest length variant of the Fiat Ducato. It measures just 541 cm (17.7 feet) in length, but the interior layout efficiently utilizes the available space to provide comfort, utility, and flexibility for life on the road.
One of the defining traits of the Schauinsland 540 is its open interior layout. There is no solid divider wall behind the driver’s cab, which is always a good choice for compact interiors, as it not only allows easy access from front to back and vice versa, but it also makes the interior feel more spacious and airier.
Instead of dedicating a large portion of the available floor space to a permanent internal bathroom, SüdBadenVan has chosen a more minimalist yet practical approach, with a functional kitchen, a generous seating and dining setup that transforms into a comfortable bed, and ample storage integrated throughout.
This configuration might seem incomplete for some, especially if they plan to adopt a nomad lifestyle full-time, but it frees up precious square footage for a larger kitchen, extra seating, and a bigger bed. However, the Schauinsland 540 doesn’t lack sanitary conveniences altogether. A Trelino composting toilet is still included in a dedicated compartment and slides out only when needed. Optional dry or sealing toilets are also available, and travelers who prefer a more conventional setup can opt for the Schauinsland 540 D , which integrates a wet bathroom.
Photo: SüdBadenVan/miniCampers The open layout allows for seamless transitions between the living, kitchen, and sleeping areas. At the front, the cab seats swivel all the way around to add extra seating space, and the nearby kitchen is well-equipped for fresh home-cooked meals.
It features a 1,800-watt induction cooktop, a stainless steel sink with a folding faucet, and a 70-liter compressor refrigerator, neatly integrated into a suspended cabinet. The water storage is deliberately kept compact and flexible. Instead of permanent tanks, the company equipped the van with a 20-liter fresh water tank and a 20-liter waste water tank, positioned directly under the sink. Both are removable, making them easier to handle when filling or emptying.
Photo: SüdBadenVan/miniCampers At the rear, the Schauinsland 540 camper van features a versatile seating and sleeping area. During the day, you get a U-shaped sofa with a round, height-adjustable table in the middle, creating a nice setup for dining, lounging, and spending time indoors.
At night, the opposing sofas can be used as two longitudinal beds measuring approximately 180 x 70 cm (70 x 27.5 inches) and 200 x 70 cm (79 x 27.5 inches), respectively, or can be combined to form a much larger sleeping surface of around 200 by 180 cm (79 by 70 inches). If more sleeping capacity is needed, an optional pop-up roof transforms the Schauinsland 540 into a four-berth camper.
Because many travelers view their vehicles not just as a means of travel , but as genuine living spaces, the aesthetics aspect is really important. The team at SüdBadenVan seems to understand its clients’ need for a homey vibe, and for this camper van, they used a combination of wooden surfaces, light finishes, and soft upholstery to create a country-house ambiance reminiscent of a small chalet on wheels.
Photo: SüdBadenVan/miniCampers The kitchen counters, cabinet fronts, and rear tabletop, for instance, are finished in Swiss stone pine, which, with its fine grain and dark knots, brings warmth to the living space. The plank-style ceiling paneling and grey felt material on the side walls further enhance the cozy, warm ambiance, while the high-quality mattresses, available with fabric or corduroy covers, add another residential touch.
The built-in cabinetry inside this van is made from waterproof bonded lightweight plywood, while the cabinet fronts and window frames feature multiplex construction with genuine Swiss stone pine veneer. The rig is designed for all-season use with 19mm Vanue insulation, vinyl flooring with impact-sound insulation, and a 2-kW Autoterm diesel parking heater with ComfortControl functionality.
For electrical independence, the camper van is equipped with an EcoFlow PowerHub, which delivers 3,600 watts of AC output (or up to 5,200 watts with X-Boost). The system incorporates an integrated charging booster and shore power charger, along with two solar charge controllers for fixed and mobile solar installations.
Photo: SüdBadenVan/miniCampers A selection of optional features is also available and includes a pop-top roof with integrated lighting and a mattress, a larger EcoFlow battery, a 5G WLAN router for internet connectivity, a Dometic FlyTec insect screen door, extra roof hatches, and more.
It’s also worth mentioning that the base vehicle comes standard with a 140-hp engine paired with a manual transmission, but buyers can upgrade to a 180-hp engine with an automatic gearbox as well. And for those who want to venture into the wilderness, an off-road package is also available, featuring all-season tires and Fiat's Traction+ system.
As for pricing, the 2027 SüdBadenVan Schauinsland 540 camper van starts at €89,000 ($99.880), but the custom options and upgrades will push the total higher.
